# transmit_oncall_schedule_override (Resource)

Puts one responder on call in place of a schedule's rotations for a period, such as covering a vacation. A schedule holds at most 1000 overrides, so delete past ones.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "transmit_oncall_schedule_override" "dana_vacation" {
  configuration_id = transmit_oncall_configuration.prod.id
  schedule_id      = transmit_oncall_schedule.primary.id
  starts_at        = "2026-12-24T00:00:00-05:00"
  ends_at          = "2026-12-27T00:00:00-05:00"
  responder_id     = transmit_oncall_responder.lee.id
  rotation_ids     = [transmit_oncall_schedule.primary.rotation_ids["Weekly"]]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `configuration_id` (String) The on-call configuration this belongs to. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `ends_at` (String) RFC 3339 with an explicit offset; after `starts_at`.
- `responder_id` (String) Who is on call instead.
- `schedule_id` (String) The schedule to override. Changing it replaces the override.
- `starts_at` (String) RFC 3339 with an explicit offset.

### Optional

- `rotation_ids` (Set of String) Rotations the override replaces, usually from `transmit_oncall_schedule.<name>.rotation_ids`. Omit to cover every rotation the schedule had when the override was created.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <configuration_id>/<schedule_id>/<override_id>
terraform import transmit_oncall_schedule_override.dana_vacation 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004
```
